name: Run kube-bench against node and master
objective: CKS › Cluster Setup + System Hardening (10% + 15%). Drill the kube-bench workflow harder than the exam: run it as a Job against node AND master, read [PASS]/[FAIL]/[WARN], then remediate every recurring finding — manifest & PKI file modes, the kubelet read-only port, the apiserver NodeRestriction plugin — plus a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Audit a worker node with kube-bench
questions.teach:
**kube-bench** audits a node against the **CIS Kubernetes Benchmark**, printing `[PASS]`, `[FAIL]`, or `[WARN]` per numbered control. Because it inspects the host's real files, run it **on the node** — as a Job with `hostPID: true` and hostPath mounts — and read findings from the pod logs.

**Gotcha:** a plain pod without `hostPID` and host mounts reads the container's filesystem, not the host, giving bogus results.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `cks-bench`, create a Job named `kube-bench` using image `aquasec/kube-bench:latest` with args `["run","--targets","node"]`, `hostPID: true`, `restartPolicy: Never`, and hostPath mounts for `/var/lib/kubelet`, `/etc/kubernetes`, and `/etc/systemd`. Wait for it to complete.

Target: Job `kube-bench` in `cks-bench` has a completed pod whose logs contain at least one of `[PASS]`, `[FAIL]`, `[WARN]`.
questions.hint: Apply a Job with `restartPolicy: Never`, `hostPID: true`, image `aquasec/kube-bench:latest`, args `["run","--targets","node"]`, and hostPath volumes for the three host paths. Then `kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\]'`.
questions.solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: { name: kube-bench, namespace: cks-bench }
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  template:
    spec:
      hostPID: true
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: kube-bench
        image: aquasec/kube-bench:latest
        command: ["kube-bench"]
        args: ["run","--targets","node"]
        volumeMounts:
        - { name: var-lib-kubelet, mountPath: /var/lib/kubelet, readOnly: true }
        - { name: etc-kubernetes, mountPath: /etc/kubernetes, readOnly: true }
        - { name: etc-systemd, mountPath: /etc/systemd, readOnly: true }
      volumes:
      - { name: var-lib-kubelet, hostPath: { path: /var/lib/kubelet } }
      - { name: etc-kubernetes, hostPath: { path: /etc/kubernetes } }
      - { name: etc-systemd, hostPath: { path: /etc/systemd } }
YAML
kubectl -n cks-bench wait --for=condition=complete job/kube-bench --timeout=120s
kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\]' | head

verification.description: Job kube-bench completed with hostPID and host mounts; logs contain CIS [PASS]/[FAIL]/[WARN]

questions.title: Audit the control plane (--targets master)
questions.teach:
`--targets node` only covers the kubelet/worker checks (CIS section 4). The control-plane checks (apiserver, scheduler, etcd — CIS section 1) live under `--targets master` and only appear when kube-bench runs **on a control-plane node** where those files exist.

**Gotcha:** a master-targets Job landing on a worker finds no control-plane files — pin it to the control-plane node with a nodeSelector + toleration.
questions.prompt:
In `cks-bench`, create a Job named `kube-bench-master` (`aquasec/kube-bench:latest`, args `["run","--targets","master"]`, `hostPID: true`, `restartPolicy: Never`, same three hostPath mounts) that is pinned to the control-plane node so it can read `/etc/kubernetes/manifests`. Wait for completion.

Target: Job `kube-bench-master` completed on the control-plane node; its logs contain a CIS **1.x** master finding (e.g. `[PASS] 1.` or `[FAIL] 1.`).
questions.hint: Add `nodeSelector: { node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: "" }` and a control-plane toleration so it lands on `$CP`. Use args `["run","--targets","master"]`. Then `kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench-master | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\] 1\.'`.

verification.description: Job kube-bench-master ran on the control plane and logged CIS section 1.x (master) findings
